And perhaps his view here is that ritual slaughtering (shechitah) for fowl is not...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the hidden light of Torah, the spiritual root of the letters and mitzvot, and the halakhic-aggadic synthesis developed in Ohr Zarua LaTzadik.
column13: At first glance, one might think that Netzach and Hod simply correspond to Chesed and Gevurah. But with respect to the power of the garments themselves, it is actually the reverse: Gevurah and Chesed. For the power that conceals Chesed so that it will not expand without limit is itself a power of Gevurah. So too, the power that conceals Gevurah is Chesed, for when Chesed is revealed, Gevurah is concealed, because the two are opposites.

column13: Sorrow (yagon) signifies deficiency, joy (simchah) signifies surplus expansion, while the median state preserves baseline equilibrium. Hence a "wise son" supplements the mother, while a "foolish son" diminishes the father, who in his elevated state requires no external completion. And as known: "If you are righteous, what do you give Him?" (Job 35:7), yet the Shechinah [the supernal Mother, matching Berakhot (35b): "'his father' is the Holy One, Blessed be He, and 'his mother' is the Congregation of Israel"] laments: "My head is heavy, My arm is heavy" over the sinner (Sanhedrin 46a).
column15: “Fifteen cubits upward did the waters prevail; and the mountains were covered.” Behold, the surging of the waters is repeated here four times: twice below the mountains and twice above the mountains, hinting that through anger traversing a person and swelling above his intellect—symbolized by the mountains—he stumbles into error even in matters below his intellect.
